issues.legal_issue: A partition suit is not incompetent for non-joinder of a person pleaded to have been adopted out when that adoption was not specifically denied and no issue was raised on it.
material_facts: The partition plaint stated that an additional son had been given in adoption and was therefore not joined as a party.
The defendants said they had no knowledge of that allegation rather than specifically denying it.
No issue on adoption was framed.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not incompetent because the person said to have been adopted out was not joined.
issues.legal_principle: Order VIII Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that an allegation of fact not specifically denied, denied by necessary implication, or stated to be not admitted is taken as admitted. Saying that the defendants had no knowledge of the pleaded adoption did not amount to a denial. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: partition_suit and adoption_pleaded and adoption_not_specifically_denied and no_adoption_issue_framed

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding seeks partition of jointly owned property.
predicates.adoption_pleaded: A party stated in the pleading that the omitted person had been adopted out of the family.
predicates.adoption_not_specifically_denied: The opposing party did not specifically deny the pleaded adoption, including by responding only that it had no knowledge of it.
predicates.no_adoption_issue_framed: The court did not frame an issue requiring determination of whether the adoption occurred.
predicates.partition_suit_not_incompetent_for_nonjo: The partition suit is not incompetent because the person said to have been adopted out was not joined.

issues.definition: When a partition suit pleads an adoption that is not specifically denied and no issue is framed on it, non-joinder of the person said to have been adopted out does not make the suit incompetent.

issues.legal_issue: Oral evidence of an adoption is admissible even when a deed recording the adoption is acknowledged but not produced.
material_facts: A witness testified to the adoption.
The witness acknowledged that a deed of adoption existed, but the deed was not produced.
The deed recorded that an adoption had taken place; it was not an instrument that itself brought the change of status into existence.
issues.conclusion: The existence and non-production of the deed did not make oral evidence of the adoption inadmissible.
issues.legal_principle: A deed of adoption that records an adoption is a piece of evidence, not an instrument that by its own force creates the adoption. Oral evidence is therefore not rendered inadmissible merely because such a deed exists but is not produced. No earlier cases or statutory provisions were relied on for this point.

rule.if: adoption_proof_proceeding and witness_testified_to_adoption and adoption_deed_records_event_only and adoption_deed_not_produced

predicates.adoption_proof_proceeding: The proceeding involves proof of whether an adoption occurred.
predicates.witness_testified_to_adoption: A witness gave oral testimony that the adoption occurred.
predicates.adoption_deed_records_event_only: The deed records an adoption that had occurred rather than itself creating the adoption.
predicates.adoption_deed_not_produced: The deed was not produced in the proceeding.
predicates.oral_evidence_admissible_to_prove_adopti: Oral evidence may be admitted to prove the adoption.

issues.definition: When a witness testifies to an adoption and an unproduced deed merely records the event, the oral testimony is admissible to prove the adoption.

issues.legal_issue: An agreement between co-owners to pay compensation for occupation of jointly owned property does not by itself create a landlord-and-tenant relationship or bring a co-ownership dispute within rent-control jurisdiction.
material_facts: The parties were co-owners holding the undivided property as tenants-in-common, and their shares had not been demarcated.
One group occupied the property, including the other group's share, under an agreement to pay compensation.
The parties did not intend the agreement to create a landlord-and-tenant relationship.
The respondents sued for compensation and partition.
issues.conclusion: The rent-control provisions did not apply, and the civil suit was not barred on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11(2) of the Bihar Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1947, placed specified claims concerning tenants before the Rent Controller and ousted civil jurisdiction for those claims. Its application required a landlord-and-tenant relationship. Co-owners holding property as tenants-in-common do not become landlord and tenant merely because one agrees to pay the other compensation for occupation. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.coownership_property_suit: The proceeding concerns rights in jointly owned property held by co-owners.
predicates.parties_are_tenants_in_common: The parties hold the property as co-owners with undivided shares.
predicates.compensation_agreement_without_intent_to: The occupying co-owners agreed to pay the others compensation, but the parties did not intend to create a landlord-and-tenant relationship.
predicates.civil_suit_not_barred_by_rent_control_la: The civil suit is not barred by rent-control law on the basis that the parties are landlord and tenant.

issues.definition: In a co-ownership property suit, an agreement to pay compensation for occupation does not bar the civil suit under rent-control law when the parties remain tenants-in-common and did not intend to create a tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: Co-owners may agree that those occupying and enjoying undivided property will pay compensation to the other co-owners, and the agreement may be enforced without proof of ouster.
material_facts: The parties jointly owned undivided property.
The parties agreed that the occupying co-owners would pay compensation to the other co-owners for their occupation and enjoyment of the property.
The occupying co-owners did not pay the agreed compensation.
The claim was to enforce the compensation agreement; the appellants argued that it was unenforceable absent ouster.
issues.conclusion: The compensation agreement was enforceable even though there had been no ouster of the other co-owners.
issues.legal_principle: Co-owners are legally competent to make arrangements on any terms for enjoyment of their undivided property. Ouster is not a necessary condition for a co-owner to claim compensation under an agreement with an occupying co-owner. No earlier cases or statutory provisions were relied on.

predicates.claim_to_enforce_coowner_compensation_ag: The proceeding seeks to enforce an agreement for compensation between co-owners.
predicates.coowners_agreed_on_terms_for_undivided_p: The co-owners made an agreement about the enjoyment of their undivided property.
predicates.occupying_coowners_agreed_to_pay_compens: The co-owners in occupation agreed to pay compensation to the other co-owners.
predicates.compensation_agreement_enforceable_witho: The compensation agreement may be enforced without proof that the other co-owners were ousted.

issues.definition: When co-owners agree that those occupying undivided property will pay compensation, the agreement may be enforced without proof of ouster.
